main_body: A wooden keg rack frame: a top beam, two rows of kegs seen end-on (round faces with metal bands) and a base rail, all drawn from the front
top_band: Rows 8-12 are a brown beam (L109, 130, then a light row 12 at L157). It grades from dark to light downward like a front face, with no separate lighter top surface and no ellipse. Below it the kegs are drawn face-on.
evidence: The beam at the top and the base rail are flat front faces. The 1-row light line at row 12 is the only edge cue, and the dark-to-light gradient above it reads as one front face rather than a top. The kegs are shown as circular end faces with no top surfaces. The middle shelf line at rows 20-21 is only 1 row, and the base rail has no visible top. No horizontal surface is readable from above, so this is a front elevation, as the guide's red 'front elevation' example shows.

style.evidence: The candidate has 13 distinct colours against 40 and 38 in the references, and a median of 13 per tile against 17 and 20. That is well below both on total palette. Edge pixels are tinted (6% neutral) and flat-fill coverage is 0%, so the outline and fills are fine. The wood ramp has about 4-5 steps and the keg shading is simple. Texture is limited to hoop and bung details. Wood grain and per-plank variation are sparse compared with the references. The piece is cleanly drawn but thinner than the Beodeul pieces, so I fail it on the much smaller palette.
